name: port-game
description: Port a Studio game to another engine, reusing its design and assets: a port plan (what maps to what), the target project from the engine's template, the assets imported (sprites, tiles, models, sounds and levels as they are), the rules rebuilt in the target, the same state hook so the same bots and checks prove it, the target's gates, a playtest against the original's, and a build.

notes.description: Anything about the port (what may change, platforms to build)

plan.title: Port plan

port.title: Port
port.prompt: Stage: port. Build the game in {{input.target}} from design/port-{{input.target}}.md, in its own folder (web: port-web/ with studio_template create, project "port-web"; godot: game/ with godot project.create; unreal: unreal project.create), reusing the assets in .studio/assets (never redraw what exists), with the same rules and the same state hook. Prove it as you go: game_bot goal on the port.

fix.title: Fix
fix.prompt:
Stage: port-fix. The port's checks failed. Fix them and prove it again with game_bot goal.

{{feedback}}

playtest.title: Playtest against the original
playtest.prompt: Stage: port-playtest. game_playtest on the port (game: its entry or project) with the goal and checks from design/port-{{input.target}}.md, then compare with the original's playtest (game_playtest report with its id): goal reached in both, similar time to the goal, no new issues. Write docs/port-playtest.md.

fix-playtest.title: Fix what differs
fix-playtest.prompt:
Stage: port-playtest-fix. Fix every BLOCKING and MAJOR difference in docs/port-playtest.md, then game_playtest again.

{{state.playtest}}

build.title: Build the port
build.prompt: Stage: port-build. Build the port (web: studio_template build with project the port's folder; godot: godot build windows; unreal: unreal package) and record it in .studio/project.json builds.

failed.title: Stopped: the port's checks still fail
